questions.stem: In a genetic diagram, what do the letters on the top and side of a Punnett square represent?

options.text: The alleles in the gametes of each parent
The phenotypes of the parents
The genotypes of the offspring
The chromosomes in the body cells

questions.explanation: The letters on the top and side of a Punnett square represent the alleles carried by the gametes (sex cells) of each parent. Each gamete carries only one allele for each gene, as chromosome number is halved during meiosis.

questions.stem: In a cross between Tt and tt, what proportion of offspring would you expect to show the recessive phenotype?

options.text: Three quarters (75%)
One half (50%)
One quarter (25%)
None

questions.explanation: From Tt x tt: possible offspring are Tt, Tt, tt, tt. Half (50%) are tt and show the recessive phenotype. The other half are Tt and show the dominant phenotype.

questions.stem: What is a pedigree diagram used for?

options.text: To compare the chromosomes of different species
To predict the genotypes of future offspring
To trace the inheritance of a trait through several generations of a family
To show the structure of a DNA molecule

questions.explanation: A pedigree diagram traces the inheritance of a particular trait through several generations of a family. It uses standard symbols to show males, females, affected individuals, and carriers, helping to determine inheritance patterns.

questions.stem: If two parents with genotypes Bb and Bb have four children, will exactly 3 show the dominant trait and 1 show the recessive?

options.text: Yes, always exactly 3:1
No, the 3:1 ratio is a probability; actual results may vary
No, all four children will show the dominant trait
Yes, but only if both parents are healthy

questions.explanation: The 3:1 ratio is a predicted probability, not a guarantee. With only 4 children, the actual ratio could be anything. Each child independently has a 3 in 4 chance of the dominant phenotype and 1 in 4 chance of the recessive.

questions.stem: When constructing a genetic diagram, why is it important to use a capital letter for the dominant allele?

options.text: Because recessive alleles cannot be represented by letters
It is a convention that clearly distinguishes dominant from recessive alleles
Because only capital letters represent alleles
Because dominant alleles are always larger

questions.explanation: Using a capital letter for the dominant allele and a lowercase letter for the recessive allele is a standard convention in genetics. This makes it easy to distinguish between the two and clearly show genotypes like BB, Bb, and bb.

questions.stem: What genotype ratio is expected from a cross between two heterozygous parents (Aa x Aa)?

options.text: 1 AA : 1 Aa : 2 aa
All Aa
1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa
2 AA : 1 Aa : 1 aa

questions.explanation: The cross Aa x Aa produces offspring in the genotype ratio 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa. This gives a phenotype ratio of 3 dominant : 1 recessive, as both AA and Aa show the dominant phenotype.

questions.stem: Why does each gamete contain only one allele for each gene?

options.text: Because gametes do not contain DNA
Because meiosis halves the chromosome number, separating allele pairs
Because gametes are produced by mitosis
Because alleles are destroyed during fertilisation

questions.explanation: Gametes are produced by meiosis, which halves the chromosome number. Since alleles are on homologous chromosomes that separate during meiosis, each gamete ends up with only one allele for each gene.
